topic.subject: social
topic.title: Socialism and the Russian Revolution
topic.scope: liberals, radicals, conservatives, socialism, February and October revolutions, Lenin, Bolsheviks, collectivisation

misconceptions.statement: Liberals in 19th century Europe were the same as modern democrats.
misconceptions.why: Students assume the word 'liberal' always implies support for universal voting rights.
misconceptions.fix: Liberals wanted a representative government but did not believe in universal adult franchise; they felt only men with property should vote.

probe.question: Did 19th-century liberals support the right of all women to vote?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because they were liberals and believed in equality.

misconceptions.root_belief: a word means its everyday modern meaning

misconceptions.statement: Marx believed that the government should simply give money to the poor.
misconceptions.why: Students often view socialism as simple charity or wealth redistribution by a king or state.
misconceptions.fix: Marx argued that workers must overthrow capitalism and take control of the means of production to create a classless society.

probe.question: How did Marx think the workers' lives would improve?
probe.wrong_answer: By the government passing laws to give them higher wages.

misconceptions.statement: The 1905 Revolution successfully removed the Tsar from power.
misconceptions.why: Students often conflate the 'dress rehearsal' of 1905 with the final revolution of 1917.
misconceptions.fix: The 1905 Revolution led to the creation of the Duma, but the Tsar remained in power and eventually dismissed the Duma.

probe.question: Who was the ruler of Russia during the start of World War I in 1914?

misconceptions.root_belief: revolutions always result in immediate regime change

misconceptions.statement: Lenin led the February Revolution from the front in Petrograd.
misconceptions.why: Lenin is the most famous figure, so students attribute all revolutionary actions to him.
misconceptions.fix: Lenin was in exile during the February Revolution; it was a spontaneous uprising of workers and soldiers.

probe.question: Where was Lenin when the Tsar abdicated in February 1917?
probe.wrong_answer: Leading the crowds at the Winter Palace.

misconceptions.root_belief: famous leaders cause every event in their era

misconceptions.statement: The April Theses were a set of demands made by the Tsar to the people.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the source of official-sounding 'theses' or 'decrees'.
misconceptions.fix: The April Theses were three demands made by Lenin: end the war, transfer land to peasants, and nationalise banks.

probe.question: What was one of the main points of Lenin's April Theses?
probe.wrong_answer: To support the Tsar's war efforts.

misconceptions.root_belief: the old ruler stays in the new government

misconceptions.statement: The 'Whites' in the Civil War were the peaceful citizens who wanted no war.
misconceptions.why: The color white is often associated with peace in modern cultural contexts.
misconceptions.fix: The 'Whites' were pro-Tsarists and anti-Bolsheviks who fought a violent civil war against the 'Reds'.

probe.question: Who were the 'Whites' fighting against in the Russian Civil War?
probe.wrong_answer: They weren't fighting; they were the peace-loving neutrals.

misconceptions.statement: The October Revolution was a massive, bloody battle involving millions of citizens.
misconceptions.why: Students imagine all 'revolutions' look like the French Revolution or cinematic war scenes.
misconceptions.fix: The October Revolution was a relatively quiet and organized takeover of government offices by Bolshevik committees.

probe.question: How did the Bolsheviks take power in October 1917?
probe.wrong_answer: Through a years-long war in the streets of every Russian city.

misconceptions.root_belief: political takeovers are always violent and loud

misconceptions.statement: Kulaks were foreign invaders who stole Russian land.
misconceptions.why: The harsh sounding name and the fact they were 'eliminated' makes students think they were outsiders.
misconceptions.fix: Kulaks were simply well-to-do Russian peasants who owned land and were targeted during collectivisation.

probe.question: Who were the Kulaks targeted by Stalin?

misconceptions.root_belief: enemies of the state must be outsiders

misconceptions.statement: Collectivisation was a system where peasants could choose to share their tools.
misconceptions.why: The word 'collective' sounds like voluntary cooperation.
misconceptions.fix: Collectivisation was a forced policy where the state took land from peasants to create large state-controlled farms (Kolkhoz).

probe.question: What happened to peasants who refused to join collective farms?
probe.wrong_answer: They were allowed to keep their small private plots.

misconceptions.root_belief: state policies are always welcomed by the poor

misconceptions.statement: The Provisional Government was led by the Bolsheviks.
misconceptions.why: Students assume the group that eventually won power must have been in charge the whole time.
misconceptions.fix: The Provisional Government was led by liberals and moderate socialists like Kerensky, whom the Bolsheviks later overthrew.

probe.question: Who did the Bolsheviks overthrow in the October Revolution?

misconceptions.root_belief: the most famous group did everything

misconceptions.statement: The Russian Revolution had no impact on countries like India.
misconceptions.why: Students often view history as isolated national stories.
misconceptions.fix: The revolution inspired many Indians; leaders like Jawaharlal Nehru and Tagore wrote about Soviet socialism.

probe.question: How did Indian nationalists react to the Russian Revolution?
probe.wrong_answer: They ignored it because it was only about Europe.

misconceptions.root_belief: national events have no international consequences

misconceptions.statement: Bloody Sunday happened because the workers attacked the Tsar's palace with weapons.
misconceptions.why: Students assume a 'bloody' event must involve a two-sided fight.
misconceptions.fix: Bloody Sunday was a peaceful procession of workers carrying a petition who were fired upon by the Tsar's police.

probe.question: What were the workers carrying during the Bloody Sunday march?
probe.wrong_answer: Guns and bombs to kill the Tsar.

misconceptions.root_belief: victims are always the intentional aggressors
misconceptions.source_hint: history education research on protest narratives
